newsitem.title: THAILAND: Rerngchai says he quit after political pressure.
newsitem.headline: Rerngchai says he quit after political pressure.

text.p: Former Bank of Thailand governor Rerngchai Marakanond said on Tuesday his decision to quit was prompted by recent public criticism of his performance and political pressure on him to leave office.

Rerngchai, who tendered his resignation on Monday after about a year in the top central bank job, said in a statement: "Like any human being...who is discouraged by sarcastic remarks and in order to protect my integrity and that of the Bank of Thailand, I would like to show my spirit by resigning from the governership."

Rerngchai said the central bank under his leadership had initiated an unprecedented number of measures to deal with Thailand's bursting economic bubble, including its decision on a de facto devaluation of the baht on July 2.
He said the central bank proposed and won government approval on July 22 for Thailand to seek assistance from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) to tackle its economic turmoil.
"(Through these measures), the long-term process of reviving the economy and strengthening financial institutions was launched," he said.
Rerngchai said he did not allow himself to be swayed by political or business interests. "My job so far has been strongly criticised and I faced consistent political pressure for me to leave office."
